messages.author: 33dc9c6d026ee296
messages.subject: R Markdown Shiny app displays well locally, and remotely on Firefox, but remotely is spotty on some other browsers
parts:
I don't know whether this is properly a 

* shinyapps.io vs. Shiny Server web hosting question,
* a `shiny` question,
* a question about browsers,
* a question about operating systems, or 
* a question about the interaction between some subset of the above four domains.

So believe me I'm not expecting immediate help on this:  I just think it's an issue worth reporting.

I have an R Markdown document, with `runtime:  shiny`.   Relevant source code is in a GitHub repo.  The document calls seven related Shiny apps.  For example, here is the code chunk for the first app:

```{r, echo=FALSE}
shinyAppDir(
  "example_sim_01/",
  options=list(
    width="100%", height=550
  )
)
```

When I run the document locally, all of the apps display correctly.  (I have tried this on Ubuntu 14.04 with Firefox, and on Mac OSX Yosemite with Safari.)

I have deployed the app to shinyapps.io.  (See http://homer.shinyapp.io/sim_tutorial_Rmd).

When I am on my Linux platform, the all of the called in the deployed app display correctly.  (On Linux I have tried this only with Firefox.

On Windows 7 and on Mac OS X I find a problem, with all of the browsers I have tried so far:

* Chrome and IE on Windows 7 (no problem seen yet with Firefox);
* Safari and Firefox on Mac OSX

The "problem" is this:  for one or more of the apps (usually some subset of apps 2-5, but occasionally app 1 or app 6 as well, never app 7), the ui appears but initial output in the main panel does not appear.  If I refresh, then some of the affected apps may display correctly.

I cannot detect any pattern for which apps will be affected on initial view, nor for which apps will be corrected upon refresh.

All tested browsers are up to date.  shiny and shinyapps are up to date.

I would have access to a Shiny Server through my college.  Once some perms are set I should be able to install the app there and test for whether it's a means-of-hosting issue (shinyapps.io vs. Shiny Server).

Based on my data so far,  I'm leaning towards it being a browser-for-platform issue.

Any thoughts?

Homer

messages.subject: Re: R Markdown Shiny app displays well locally, and remotely on Firefox, but remotely is spotty on some other browsers
parts:
One other piece of information that might be of use.

The seven apps are similar in nature and hence in code; in particular, the initial plot on each one of them comes from an output object named output$initialGraph.  On the chance that this somehow causes the objects to get in each other's way when the app is rendered to HTML, on a testing branch here I assigned distinct names to the initial graph objects in each app.

The deployed app is at:  http://homer.shinyapps.io/bugtest.  Unfortunately the problem persists.

Homer

I started by correcting input$takesample to input.takesample in the ui for app #3 in the document, then deployed.  I have checked quite a few times on several browsers.  No more problems!

I left in the duplicated crosstab outputs (both within the eighth app in the document). They were there to illustrate the ill effects of duplication.

Interestingly, there documents still contains many duplicate output items ACROSS apps, but they do not appear to pose a problem, in any browser, in any deployment method.

So as best I can tell, it all came down to how shinyapps.io reacted to input$name in a Javascript conditional.  Thanks for spotting the cause of the problem.

Regards,
Homer
